ops.title: E2 spike — Apple `container machine` boots NixOS with an external kernel + NO guest initrd on a read-only root, so system.etc.overlay can't work (it's initrd-only); the fix is a pre-init /sbin/init tmpfs wrapper. m1b image built + nspawn-verified to mult

ops.body:
E2 = booting a wholesale NixOS OCI image as an Apple `container machine`. Two boot gates, both rooted in the same fact: Apple boots the guest rootfs with its **own external kernel and NO guest initrd** (per machine.nix design + confirmed: `boot.isContainer=true`, toplevel has no `/initrd`), on a **read-only root**.

- **Gate 1 (pre-init, `configureDns` abort):** Apple writes `/etc/resolv.conf` during bootstrap before `/sbin/init` runs. The minimal nix2container rootfs (only `/sbin/init` symlink in copyToRoot) has **no `/etc` at all** → write fails. Fix: bake `/etc` + a regular `/etc/resolv.conf` target into the image.
- **Gate 2 (stage-2, NixOS activation):** stage-2 init + `activate` rewrite `/etc` (`setup-etc.pl`, `update-users-groups.pl`), `/bin`, `/usr`, `/root`, `/home`; systemd then needs `/var`,`/tmp`,`/run`,`/sys`. All fail on read-only root. Read-only `/nix/store` is FINE (NixOS default; stage-2 `chown -f`/`chmod -f` tolerate it). NixOS's `container=oci` boot path **skips** `mount -o remount,rw /`, assuming the manager gave it writable paths — Apple doesn't.

**`system.etc.overlay.enable` CANNOT fix this** — its overlay mounts live entirely in `boot.initrd.systemd` (asserts `boot.initrd.systemd.enable`), i.e. an initrd Apple never loads. The team lead's suggested lever was architecturally impossible.

**The initrd-free fix (implemented):** replace `/sbin/init` with a pre-init wrapper that mounts `proc/dev/sys/run` + tmpfs on `/etc /var /tmp /root /home /bin /usr /nix/var`, then `exec`s the real `${toplevel}/init`. Mountpoints must be **pre-baked** (read-only root can't `mkdir` them). Lives in the flake as `mkImageRO` → `packages.aarch64-linux.imageRO` (tag m1b), reusing the m1 toplevel. Flake on hermes `/root/container-spike/flake.nix` (backup: `flake.nix.bak-preRO`).

**Verified via `systemd-nspawn --read-only`:** reached `multi-user.target`, `is-system-running: running`, **zero failed units**, `/etc` set up on read-only root. nspawn's `/dev/kmsg` EPERM + `/dev/pts`,`/dev/shm` mount failures are nspawn capability restrictions, not read-only-root issues.

**AUTHORITATIVE Apple-machine boot result (m1b, 2026-07-15):** `container machine create m1blocal:v1` **consistently passes `configureDns`** — the baked `/etc/resolv.conf` fix CLEARED gate 1 (the original blocker that killed m1/hermes-spike). It now fails one step later at a NEW machine-specific requirement: Apple `container machine` execs **`/sbin.machine/init`** (not `/sbin/init`) → `failed to exec [/sbin.machine/init] No such file or directory`. So the wholesale-NixOS-machine path is MORE viable than the first attempt showed, but hits successive machine-specific conventions. Next fix: put the pre-init wrapper at `/sbin.machine/init` (a one-line copyToRoot change) — may reveal gate N+1. NOTE: reference the LOCAL image (`container image tag m1b m1blocal:v1`) — a bare `m1b:latest` makes container try to PULL from docker.io (401). This is the BONUS path; E1 (socktainer chain) carries the sandbox gate, so E2 was not pursued to a full boot. See [[apple-container-prototype-verdict]], [[hermes-model-plane-egress]].
